'''Gregory Abelevich Freiman''' ({{Langx|ru|Григорий Абелевич Фрейман}}; 3 July 1926 – 19 September 2024) was a Russian and Israeli mathematician known for his work in [[additive number theory]], in particular, for proving [[Freiman's theorem]].<ref>{{cite book|mr=2522038|last=Ruzsa|first=Imre Z.|chapter=Sumsets and structure|title=Combinatorial number theory and additive group theory|pages=87&ndash;210|series= Adv. Courses Math. CRM Barcelona|publisher=Birkhäuser Verlag|location=Basel|year=2009|doi=10.1007/978-3-7643-8962-8|isbn=978-3-7643-8961-1}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|first=M. B.|last=Nathanson|title=Additive Number Theory: Inverse Problems and the Geometry of Sumsets|series=Graduate Texts in Mathematics|volume=165|publisher=Springer-Verlag|year= 1996}}</ref> He was a professor emeritus in [[Tel Aviv University]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.math.tau.ac.il/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=3&Itemid=13|title=Senior Faculty Members|publisher=Tel Aviv University|access-date=2012-03-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131122014318/http://www.math.tau.ac.il/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=3&Itemid=13|archive-date=2013-11-22|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Biography==
Freiman was born in [[Kazan]] on 3 July 1926. He graduated from [[Moscow University]] in 1949, and obtained his [[Candidate of Sciences]] in [[Kazan University]] in 1956. From 1956 he worked in [[Elabuga]], and in 1965 he defended his [[Doctor of Sciences]] degree under the joint supervision of [[Alexander Gelfond]], Alexey G. Postnikov, and [[Alexander Buchstab]].<ref name="mg">{{mathgenealogy|id=33517}}</ref> From 1967 he worked in [[Vladimir, Russia|Vladimir]],<ref>{{cite book|chapter-url=http://217.23.189.98/lib/elib/Data/Content/128734778645781250/|last1=Гильмуллин|first1=М.Ф.|last2=Иванова|first2=В.Ф.|last3=Сабирова|first3=Ф.М.|chapter=История физико-математического университета в лицах|script-title=ru:=Проблемы исследования и преподавания дисциплин физико-математического цикла в вузе и школе: Материалы Всероссийской научно-практической конференции|location=Елабуга|publisher=Изд-во ЕГПУ|year=2008|language=Russian|access-date=2012-03-07|archive-date=2017-07-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170724101857/http://217.23.189.98/lib/elib/Data/Content/128734778645781250/|url-status=dead}}</ref> and later in Kalinin (now [[Tver]]).

In the 1970s and early 1980s Freiman participated in the [[refusenik]] movement. His [[samizdat]] essay ''It seems I am a Jew'', described the discrimination against Jewish mathematicians in the Soviet Union.<ref>{{cite journal|journal=Science|year=1978|volume=202|issue=4373|pages=1167&ndash;1170|doi=10.1126/science.202.4373.1167|title=Anti-Semitism Alleged in Soviet Mathematics|pmid=17735390 | last1 = Kolata | first1 = GB|bibcode=1978Sci...202.1167B}}</ref> It was published in the US in 1980.<ref>{{cite book|title=It Seems I Am a Jew: A Samizdat Essay on Soviet Mathematics|last1=Freiman|first1=Grigori|author-link1=Gregory Freiman|translator-last1=Nathanson|translator-first1=Melvyn B.|translator-link1=Melvyn B. Nathanson|location=Carbondale|publisher=Southern Illinois University Press|year=1980}}</ref>

Later, Freiman was driven out of Russia for his different views. He chose Israel as his new home country, leaving his son, daughter and wife. In Israel he became professor in Tel Aviv University and remarried.{{citation needed|date=July 2024}}

Freiman died on 19 September 2024, at the age of 98.
